Synopsis:
SpaceX (SPCX.O) stock edged up 1.4% on heavy volume as its first post-IPO lockup expiry added 911.5 million shares to the float. Despite the modest session gain, shares remain ~14% below the $135 IPO price following a sharp sell-off triggered by a disappointing earnings report revealing steep operating losses and heavy AI infrastructure spending. Subsequent lockup releases through December 8 will expand the tradeable float to ~40%; Musk's 60% stake stays locked until mid-2027. The stock has lost over 25% since its June 12 debut while the Nasdaq Composite gained ~2%. Bulls cite SpaceX's long-term disruption potential; bears flag dilution risk, cost overruns, and continued insider selling pressure.
